segments.content:
Chapter 21: An Agreement on Qianjiang University

Some things, if said by adults, would be unseemly.

But if said by a child, it's just childish talk, a sign that the kid is still young and doesn't know any better.

Relying on his 15 years of age, Li Luo glanced at his own mother, whose smile was on the verge of breaking free, and continued to say cheerfully:

"I was pretty lucky this time. Auntie, did you know? My language arts essay even got a perfect score. Many schools photocopied it to show their students."

"And because of this exceptional performance, the school made an exception and awarded me a certificate for Outstanding Graduate."

"Only eleven people in the whole school got one. It's quite rare."

This string of childish boasting from Li Luo made Zhang Xuefen's face turn red then white.

But as an elder, she couldn't bring herself to bicker with a child. In the end, she could only force a stiff expression, avoiding Lin Xiuhong's annoying smile, and look at Li Guohong beside her, asking with a strained smile:

"Your family's Li Luo did so well this time?"

"He did," Li Guohong replied amicably, with no intention of showing off or rubbing it in their faces. "He got lucky, too. A classmate helped him review his lessons."

"Our two families are quite fated this time, with both our kids getting into Fuyi High in the same year."

"Once they're in high school, Li Luo and Wei Chun will have to keep working hard, striving to get into a good university in the future."

"That's right." Wei Dongrong chimed in, a cheerful smile on his face. "They both have to work hard."

With that, he took a red envelope from his pocket and handed it to Li Luo. "Here. Anyone who can get into Fuyi High, I'm sure it's not just luck. Li Luo, take this. Wei Chun will have much to learn from you in the future."

"Thank you, Uncle." Li Luo politely accepted the red envelope.

On the other side, Li Guohong also timely took out a red envelope and handed it to Wei Chun.

After the two sides exchanged some praises, Li Guohong's family saw Wei Dongrong and the others out of the private room.

Leaving the private room and walking down the restaurant corridor, Zhang Xuefen's expression immediately darkened, her heart aching terribly.

Then, she couldn't help but slap her son's shoulder hard, questioning through gritted teeth, "You knew about that Li Luo's score all along, didn't you? Why didn't you tell me clearly beforehand?"

Wei Chun instinctively shrank back, lowering his head to look at the floor, and said in a low voice, "You didn't ask..."

"You're making me so mad." Zhang Xuefen was fuming, her chest heaving with anger.

The thought of Lin Xiuhong's beaming smile earlier made her heart feel congested.

She had always thought that the son she had raised, with his excellent grades, had always kept Lin Xiuhong's son suppressed.

But now, the tables had been turned by that boy Li Luo?!

555 points!

And a perfect score on the language arts essay!

Was that a score that kid could achieve?

"Did Xiuhong's family pull some strings, leaking the actual test papers to Li Luo or something?" Zhang Xuefen said with malicious speculation.

"That's enough." Hearing her say this, Wei Dongrong immediately frowned. "I've told you before, don't be so petty."

"Their family just runs a breakfast shop. It's only because the Li family is large that they have some decent connections in the district."

"What are our family's circumstances now? Do you need to compare yourself to them all the time?"

"The score is right there, it's a fact. Don't discuss this kind of thing anymore."

Being told off by Wei Dongrong like this, Zhang Xuefen immediately fell silent, becoming as docile as a cat, instantly reverting from her bristling state.

As they were about to reach the door of their own private room, Zhang Xuefen asked in a low voice, "If their family isn't investing in our project, what are they planning to use the money for?"

"They said they want to buy an apartment," Wei Dongrong said. "The housing prices in the city have been falling for half a year now. I don't know what they're thinking. Buying a house at a time like this, are they hoping to buy at the bottom?"

"Buying a house?" Zhang Xuefen was also stunned for a moment, then couldn't help but mock, "Their family only has that little bit in savings. They'd have to take out a loan to buy a house, right?"

"That's why I said I can't figure it out," Wei Dongrong said, shaking his head. "But it's not like we're short of their bit of money anyway."

As they spoke, they returned to their private room.

Zhang Xuefen was already turning things over in her mind, planning to ask around later to find out where Lin Xiuhong's family was planning to buy a house.

...

"Keep it, you don't have to give it to me."

In the restaurant's private room, Li Luo handed the red envelope that his uncle, Wei Dongrong, had given him to his mother.

Unexpectedly, Lin Xiuhong waved her hand, telling him to keep it himself. "I've already put away your previous red envelopes for you. Keep this one for yourself as spending money."

Li Luo raised his eyebrows. "Mom, has the sun risen from the west today?"

"What do you mean by that, you little brat?" Lin Xiuhong glanced at him and pretended to take the red envelope back. "Is that any way to talk?"

"Hey! Hey, hey, hey!" Li Luo deftly twisted his body away and quickly stuffed the red envelope into his pants pocket. "You said you'd give it to me, you can't go back on your word."

"Just take it." Lin Xiuhong rolled her eyes at him, then a smile touched her lips, her mood exceptionally cheerful.

After all, ever since she got married, whenever she encountered Zhang Xuefen's sharp tongue, Lin Xiuhong never came out on top.

Today, her own son, Li Luo, with his chattering mouth, had for the first time helped Lin Xiuhong even the score, allowing her, as a mother, to re-experience the joy of raising a child for a rare moment.

So this is how great it feels when your own child does well in school?

At this thought, Lin Xiuhong didn't forget to remind him, "You've taken the red envelope, and we're buying you a house. If you go to Fuyi High and mess around like you used to, I'll deal with you."

"Don't worry, don't worry." Li Luo patted his chest, then pointed to Ying Chanxi beside him and chuckled. "Ying Chanxi said before that as long as I get into Fuyi High, I can definitely get into Qianjiang University. If I don't get in in the end, Mom, you can go settle the score with her."

Ying Chanxi was eating a fruit platter. Hearing Li Luo's words, she immediately swallowed the watermelon in her mouth. "I was encouraging you. Who gave you a guarantee?"

"You haven't lost an ounce of your shamelessness," Lin Xiuhong said with a disgusted look, then added, "Is Qianjiang University something you can get into just by saying so?"

Qianjiang University, located on the banks of the Yin River in the Yinjiang District of Yuhang City, Qianjiang Province, was the top university in the entire province, bar none.

Across the whole country, it was also a comprehensive 985 and 211 Double First-Class university that was stably ranked in the top five.

Although Li Luo had successfully gotten into Fuyi High, Lin Xiuhong had never really thought her son could reach the level of Qianjiang University.

After all, among their relatives, it was only once in a while that one or two kids got into Fuyi High.

But there hadn't been a single one who had managed to get into Qianjiang University.

If Li Luo could get in, it would truly be a miracle, like smoke rising from their ancestral graves.

But thinking of this, Lin Xiuhong couldn't help but look at Ying Chanxi and suddenly realized, "Speaking of which, Xixi's mother graduated from Qianjiang University, didn't she?"

At this mention, Ying Chanxi's expression froze for a moment, and she fell into a recollection, nodding lightly. "Yes... Mom was a graduate of Qianjiang University."

"To get into Qianjiang University in that era was really impressive," Lin Xiuhong said, then added, "But Xixi, with your grades, you could actually get into those two universities in the capital, right?"

"Qianjiang University is the best choice," Ying Chanxi said, shaking her head with a blossoming smile. "There are no other options."

Turning to look at his childhood friend's profile, Li Luo sighed, then said, "Then I'll reluctantly condescend to go to Qianjiang University to keep you company."

"You said that?" Ying Chanxi turned her head to meet Li Luo's gaze, her eyes sparkling brightly. "No take-backs."

"It's a deal," Li Luo chuckled.

The college entrance exam was still three years away. He could definitely manage to recall and replicate the exam papers from back then.

...

After the school promotion banquet ended, Li Luo entered the peaceful routine of summer vacation.

There was no homework required for the summer between junior and senior high, so his time was entirely his to arrange.

He now woke up at just past three in the morning to go help his parents at the shop, then came home at noon to catch up on sleep.

In the afternoons and evenings, he would be cooped up in Ying Chanxi's study, tapping away at the keyboard.

Occasionally, he would ask Zhao Rongjun out to play basketball, reacquainting himself with this young body that had an inexhaustible supply of energy.

He thought back to his past life. Because of his long hours sitting while writing web novels right after graduating from college, his weight had soared to eighty or ninety kilograms. Later, he stayed up late working on short dramas and writing scripts, relying on takeout every day.

Later still, he would set up a stall at nine at night, stir-frying rice noodles by the roadside until three in the morning before closing, and then spend the daytime riding his small electric scooter to deliver food all over the city.

By the time he was 35, his body was already wrecked.

Now, back at the age of 15, he could leap nimbly on the court, weaving and dodging, playing for a whole afternoon without feeling tired.

Li Luo felt that this kind of life was truly wonderful.

However, as his parents signed the mortgage and went through the lending procedures to acquire Third Grandpa's house, Li Luo was also writing earnestly, hoping his first novel could somewhat ease the family's burden.

He did want to find some unorthodox ways to make quick money, but first, he didn't have much capital, and second, his status as a minor made it impossible to operate.

He could only do his humble best.

And just as Li Luo was enjoying his summer vacation, far away in Changning City, at the Wenyue Group, an editor named Qian Zhou was waiting for the backend data to refresh.

Hongdou, the chief editor of the Metropolitan genre, glanced at the time and instructed the editors in his group, "Yesterday's reader follow-up data is about to come out. Everyone submit three books for the Sanjiang Recommendation to me before noon. If any have five hundred follow-ups, add a special note."

The Sanjiang Recommendation was the best recommendation spot a book could get during its free new book period.

Out of hundreds of books in the same period, only about ten would qualify for this selection.

As a new editor, Qian Zhou's authors were of mixed quality. Unlike veteran editors who had one or two top-tier authors under their belt to guarantee their performance, he didn't have that safety net.

So, facing the weekly Sanjiang Recommendation, Qian Zhou felt somewhat nervous.

In contrast, the female editor next to him, Qing Yue, appeared relaxed, seemingly very confident about securing a Sanjiang spot this time.

Qian Zhou naturally knew the reason for this.

This editor, Qing Yue, had arrived half a year before him. In the past few months, leveraging her knowledge of Korean entertainment, she had gathered many authors skilled in writing Korean entertainment novels.

In recent years, the Korean entertainment wave had swept the country, stirring up one frenzy after another in the gossip world.

Web novels, as a form of commercial writing that chases trends, naturally followed suit. Many excellent Korean entertainment novels emerged, at one point occupying half of the metropolitan entertainment category.

Now, among new books in the metropolitan category, for every ten related to entertainment, eight were about Korean entertainment, and their stats were quite good.

Chinese entertainment novels were somewhat in decline.

Not to mention fictional entertainment in an alternate world!

But Qian Zhou didn't usually follow Korean entertainment news, nor did he watch K-dramas or follow those idols, so he rarely signed Korean entertainment novels.

Among the new books this period, there were only two entertainment novels he was optimistic about that had decent stats.

One was "Sleeping Early Makes You Taller's" *The文艺年代 (Wényì Niándài - The Artsy Era)*, which was about the arthouse film era of the sixth-generation directors at the turn of the century. It was written with considerable flavor.

The other was "Reignite's" *我真不是明星 (Wǒ Zhēn Bú Shì Míngxīng - I'm Really Not a Star)*, an alternate world entertainment story with three progressing plotlines of music, literary creation, and television dramas. It was consistently satisfying, and the plot pacing was excellent.

"Oh ho~" The editor next to him, Qing Yue, suddenly let out a joyful laugh. "This *Korean Entertainment Max Level Strategy* under me had 780 follow-ups last week. The Sanjiang spot should be secure, right?"

Hearing Qing Yue's words, Qian Zhou's heart tightened.

The metropolitan category only had about two or three Sanjiang Recommendation slots each week.

If Qing Yue's book took one, and another went to a popular subgenre like officialdom or traditional power fantasy, then the books he had would be in jeopardy.

With this in mind, Qian Zhou quickly refreshed the backend and checked the reader follow-up data for the books he was managing.

*The Artsy Era* — 507 follow-ups.

It surpassed five hundred!

What a pity... Qian Zhou was both happy and disappointed. This very flavorful Chinese entertainment novel had run into the currently trending Korean entertainment novel next door. It was somewhat regrettable.

Thinking this, Qian Zhou looked further down, and his spirits instantly lifted.

*I'm Really Not a Star*

— 1078 follow-ups!

It actually exceeded one thousand?
